Rarity.maps_to: Potion.rarity = 'uncommon' (potions.py:606), read by shop.MerchantPotionEntry pricing and by potion_pools.POTION_POOL's rarity bucket (potion_pools.py:38-65)
Rarity.rationale: EXECUTED, not asserted: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` extracts PotionRarity from every C# model and diffs it against the sim class attribute over all 51 units and reports 0 mismatches. Rarity is observable in the sim (it sets the shop price and the reward-roll bucket), so this is a behavioural verdict rather than a field copy.

Usage.maps_to: no explicit attribute; the sim's only potion-use entry point is CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:583-616), which cannot be reached outside a combat
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.CombatOnly means the game's Use button is live only during a fight. The sim reaches that by construction: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds exactly one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, on CombatState, and the conformance driver only dispatches the recording's UsePotion command inside a live fight (conformance/combat_driver.py:16,263-289). The absence of a `usage` attribute is therefore not a dropped guard for this unit -- but it IS a real gap for the four AnyTime potions, which is where the divergence is filed (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice).

TargetType.maps_to: no attribute -- `targeted` stays False, so CombatState.use_potion passes target=None (combat.py:608) and the potion applies to ctx.player (potions.py:609-614)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.AnyPlayer in a single-player run always resolves to the owner: PotionModel.EnqueueManualUse defaults `target` to `Owner.Creature` when it is a valid target (PotionModel.cs:240-243) and IsValidTarget's Self/AnyPlayer arms accept exactly that creature (PotionModel.cs:280-287). The multiplayer half -- AnyPlayer letting you throw the potion at an ally, and CanThrowAtAlly (PotionModel.cs:381-388) gating it on `RunState.Players.Count > 1` -- is out of scope by the shared contract and noted in maps_to rather than verdicted as a divergence.

CanBeGeneratedInCombat.rationale: The third and last of the C# overrides (executed grep: FairyInABottle.cs:19, FruitJuice.cs:20, RegenPotion.cs:22), and the sim's set is exactly those three ids. The port's own docstring says so (potions.py:601-602) and the code agrees, which is the check PROMPT.md bug class 24 asks for. Applied by generate_random_potion_in_combat (potion_pools.py:138-145) and not by the out-of-combat form, matching PotionFactory.cs:60-65 vs :31-34.

ExtraHoverTips.maps_to: no counterpart; the sim has no hover-tip surface
ExtraHoverTips.rationale: ExtraHoverTips / HoverTipFactory / PotionModel.HoverTip are the potion tooltip's keyword lines. Waived under the shared contract's presentation exclusion, not under any unreachability claim.

OnUse (protected override, RegenPotion.c.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<RegenPower>(ctx, target, 5, Owner.Creature, null)` -> `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, player, RegenPower, 5, applier=player)`. Same class, amount, applier. RegenPower is audit/records/power/regen.json's.

guards.what: N1: Regen Potion is CombatOnly even though it is one of the three healing-adjacent exclusions
guards.rationale: Worth pinning because the other two CanBeGeneratedInCombat=false potions are AnyTime (fruit_juice) and Automatic (fairy_in_a_bottle), so it would be easy to assume the two properties travel together. They do not: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` puts regen_potion in the CombatOnly bucket, and RegenPotion.cs:18 confirms it. The sim therefore has no AnyTime gap for this unit, only the shared wrapper one.

guards.what: W4: PotionModel.cs:324-331 brackets OnUse in BeginCardOrPotionEffect/EndCardOrPotionEffect and the sim has no re-entrancy depth counter
guards.issue: CombatManager.cs:889's `!IsExecutingCardOrPotionEffect(player)` is what stops a nested effect from triggering the empty-hand check early, and PotionModel.cs:324-331 is what puts a potion inside that bracket. The sim has no counterpart anywhere. DORMANT for the same reason audit/records/relic/unceasing_top.json G2 is dormant -- the ported cards that auto-play another card mid-resolution (cards/cascade.py:58, cards/colorless_skills.py:117) do not touch the draw pile between the inner and outer ends -- but recorded separately because the OUTER frame here is a potion, so a fix that brackets only card plays would leave this half open. What would make it live: any ported potion or card that empties the hand and then moves the draw pile from inside a nested auto-play.
